The longest river in the world is the Nile River.

To help understand the concept of inflation theory in cosmology, imagine a raisin bread dough rising in an oven. Before baking, the dough is small and dense, with raisins (representing galaxies) close together. As the dough bakes and expands rapidly, the space between the raisins increases dramatically. The raisins themselves don't move through the dough; rather, the dough (space) between them stretches. Similarly, inflation theory suggests that the early universe expanded incredibly fast, stretching the fabric of space itself and pushing distant regions far apart, much like the increasing distance between raisins in rising bread. This rapid expansion explains why the universe appears uniform and flat on large scales today.
